rationale: EU ADS type-approval rules are dedicated and UNECE technical harmonisation is advanced, while lawful operation, actors and infrastructure remain partly national and fragmented.
bridge: Art 34bis agency/deeming; Art 39 equivalence/exemption; national operational law remains necessary
sensitivity: Road/actor/liability plausibly N1–N2; technical and international remain N3.
robust_conclusion: Technical/international-leading configuration survives all plausible ±1 recoding.
caveat: This is a supranational baseline, not a self-contained road-operation jurisdiction.

rationale: The 2024 Act creates dedicated responsible actors and authorisation architecture; 2026 APS permits enable passenger-service deployment while the full authorisation framework and final safety principles are still being implemented.
family: Actor / institutional-leading configuration with staged operational permitting
bridge: APS permit bridge before full 2027 AV Act implementation
sensitivity: Operation N2–N3; actor/liability N2–N3; international N1–N2.
robust_conclusion: Actor/institution-leading configuration survives plausible recoding; legal institutionalisation precedes routine general deployment.
caveat: General full-Act implementation is planned for 2027; APS is a targeted early route, not proof that all AV use is N3.

rationale: Croatia combines EU technical approval with dedicated road-traffic rules, remote/intervention actors, owner enforcement duties and a mandatory service-level real-world validation procedure before public passenger transport.
bridge: Mandatory real-world service validation on a registered sample vehicle before passenger service
sensitivity: Liability N2–N3; infrastructure N1–N2; international N2–N3.
robust_conclusion: Deployment-assurance configuration remains robust under conservative recoding.
caveat: Civil liability and quantitative retesting/change-control rules remain less clear than traffic-offence and service-assurance rules.

rationale: EU technical approval can reach N3, but current Slovak law still relies mainly on § 49 conditional test operation for AV/FAV; dedicated general operator/control-centre/fully automated deployment rules are proposed in print 1329 but are not yet law.
bridge: § 49 test-operation permit; narrower ADV operational regime
sensitivity: Road/actor/behaviour plausibly N1–N2 because of permits and the narrower automated-delivery-vehicle regime; technical stays N3.
robust_conclusion: Testing-permit / technical-leading configuration persists under plausible recoding and after the 1 September 2026 trial-focused amendment.
caveat: Snapshot is 25 August 2026. Print 1329 passed first reading but committee deadlines fall in September; Act 131/2026 is adopted but effective only from 1 September 2026.

rationale: France combines EU vehicle approval with a dedicated automated-road-transport-system regime requiring safety demonstration for the technical system and deployed route or zone, qualified independent assessment, remote-intervention qualifications, safety management and a formal service-organiser decision before operation.
family: Deployment-assurance configuration – system safety-case / organiser-decision variant
bridge: Prior safety demonstration + qualified-body opinions + organiser decision of mise en service
sensitivity: Liability N2-N3; infrastructure N1-N2; international N2-N3.
robust_conclusion: Deployment-assurance configuration remains robust, with a safety-case/organiser-decision gate rather than Croatia’s service-test gate.
caveat: Dedicated criminal responsibility is clear; civil-liability allocation is less comprehensively AV-specific and is therefore coded conservatively at N2.

rationale: The amendment broadens/adjusts § 49 trial mechanics but does not itself create a general deployment/operator regime.

regime_label: Slovakia if print 1329 enacted substantially as proposed
rationale: Would move Slovakia from test-permit accommodation toward dedicated institutionalisation, while infrastructure and cross-border operational recognition would remain less mature.
